newsitem.title: USA: Two more independent energy companies in talks. [CORRECTED 20:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Two more independent energy companies in talks. [CORRECTED 20:20 GMT]

text.p: On Monday independent natural gas producer, New York-based Belco Oil & Gas Corp bid $15.00 per share for Wichita's Hugoton Energy Corp.

The announcement comes a week after Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp and American Exploration Co said they would form a larger company better able to fund exploration and increase their recognition on Wall Street.
Belco said the main reason for its proposed merger was to increase its share float as 80 percent is owned by insiders.
"We are incredibly overcapitalised, we are debt free and have $31 (corrects figure from $38) million in cash and that is not recognised by Wall Street," said Belco spokeswoman Myra Turoff.

The company has 31.5 million shares in issue and it was trading up 1 at 21 in mid-morning trade, making a market capitalisation of around $660 million, Hugoton's market capitalisation is $280 million.

Belco already owns 14.9 percent of Hugoton and if the merger goes ahead at $15 per share (corrects by inserting dropped passage), the blended price it will pay is $14.33 per share, compared with the $14 at which Hugoton is trading.

Hugoton's chief financial officer Mark Womble said that the company had no comment on the unsolicited offer, but analysts say that small exploration and production companies have a hard time getting recognition.

"There are more than 20 independents with a market capitalisation of more than $1.0 billion and smaller than that, it is difficult to justify big fund managers getting into the stock," said Christopher Eades, analyst at UBS Securities.
Hugoton earlier this year withdrew an offering of six million shares due to poor stockmarket conditions.
Until now, Belco has grown by the drillbit but says that its operations are conducted in a very conservative way and using joint ventures.
"Unlike other companies, we drill sequentially and we have just two rigs drilling," Turoff said.
On Friday, Chesapeake Energy Corp said it would take a $150-$200 million write-down after disappointing drilling results in the Louisiana Austin Chalk, the same region drilled by Belco.
Hugoton has a $50 million drilling programme for this year, of which $20 million is for exploration.
Over the past five years Hugoton has replaced one and a half times annual production with exploration and three and a half times with acquisitions.
Analysts say that growing by the drillbit is more risky than buying and proving up reserves.
"Although it is less risky to buy reserves, there is typically less upside than exploration," said Eades.
Belco's main assets are in the Austin Chalk of Louisiana, while Hugoton's has a strong presence in the Kansas Hugoton natural gas field and in the Oklahoma and Texas panhandles.
"We need to offset our short life, high producing reserves in the Austin Chalk with the longer life reserves owned by Hugoton," said Turoff.
The oil and gas sector has seen a raft of friendly mergers, but last week Union Pacific Resources Group Inc made a hostile bid for Pennzoil Co. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
